finding: Shared and compact gathers admitted output backing but omitted retained typed-array views. A first anonymous metadata charge also retained obsolete charges through repeated union compaction.
fix: Forecast backing and retained views together for shared/compact selection, and include both in the measured compact-versus-shared decision.
Use existing child-stage admission for scoped borrowed gather so failure rolls back the whole output without disturbing existing allocations.
Associate each view charge with its actual typed array; existing compaction provenance can release obsolete views with their backing.
Share one index buffer/view across text and nested columns; avoid Object.entries/Object.values arrays in gather planning and construction.

validation.workerConcurrency: Only file startup serialized; in-test concurrent queries unchanged.
validation.expandedLocalFixture: 29 scan-adapter tests pass, including four small/large and direct/generic gather cases.

evidence: Exact caps, cap-minus-one failure, empty arrays, repeated/null selections, sibling pools, timestamp96 planes, nested dictionary validity and detached numeric precision.
Repeated union compaction runs 512 selections for each numeric/text/binary/struct/list shape without accumulated obsolete view charges.
Real Parquet and native R2 fixtures each cover 9/900-row inputs and direct/generic scans, proving both shared and compact selected output survives scanner shutdown and releases to zero.
Existing HTTP and Worker fixtures are distinct from the local gather benchmark; current live-cloud validation is not claimed.

benchmark.scope: Local allocation scaling with borrowed inputs excluded; timings do not establish a before/after speedup.

boundaries: Batch/vector records, planner objects, temporary copy subarray views and other conversion helpers remain separate open accounting gaps.
